scope: Four separate Admin Chrome profiles plus independent Owner/Super Admin; actual local Worker and established disposable D1

checks.name: Four isolated Admin profiles create and edit independent requests offline
Four-way barrier release, lost committed response, partial prefix and unchanged-ID recovery
A virgin browser CREATE and concurrent duplicate submissions share one atomic receipt
Two Admins race an offline edit; conflict keeps both versions while independent drafts sync
Owner finalization cannot be overwritten by older Admin offline items
Competing Owner and Super Admin offline closures retain one winner and one conflict
Offline payment duplicate delivery and QR duplicate acceptance stay idempotent during recovery
Mutated scopes and foreign direct IDs are rejected after concurrent synchronization
All profiles retain immutable operations and conflict snapshots with independent acknowledgements

scenarios.scenario: Four Admins create different requests simultaneously
scenarios.evidence: P5-01/02: four independent profiles create distinct offline drafts; their first CREATE requests are all held at a browser network barrier, then released together. Four distinct server requests result. Release acknowledgements span 120 ms.

scenarios.scenario: Each Admin adds/removes products and changes quantities offline
scenarios.evidence: P5-01: each adds two products, queues CREATE, changes the retained product quantity to 2/3/4/5, removes the second product and queues dependent EDIT, with no network. Separate IndexedDB outboxes retain all eight identities and the CREATE→EDIT dependencies.

scenarios.scenario: All four reconnect and synchronize concurrently
scenarios.evidence: P5-02: four outstanding browser sync requests released together; remaining operations/recovery use the real application sync controls and Worker/D1. Two unaffected profiles finish while the faulted profiles remain pending.
P5-02/03/09 and SQL audit: the four primary requests each have one CREATE receipt. All eight expected final requests exist; no unexpected request or duplicate active quotation exists.

P5-02: Admin 1's successful CREATE response is inspected at Chrome's response stage, then discarded before client delivery; connection goes offline. The server commit exists but the browser retains the operation as pending. Retry uses the identical operation ID and returns the original receipt/request; its dependent edit then completes. This is lost-response/network-failure simulation, not a wall-clock timeout benchmark.

P5-03: one previously uncommitted browser CREATE and three simultaneous direct copies using that same authenticated device/payload produce one winning commit and three replays, all pointing to one request. P5-07 repeats concurrent same-identity delivery for payment and QR acceptance.

scenarios.scenario: Unique operation IDs and atomic sync receipts
scenarios.evidence: P5-03/09 plus SQL: 21 distinct durable operation IDs, exactly one receipt for each of 16 acknowledgements, no receipts for five conflicts. Every receipt matches its completed request revision and audit event. No partial receipt/request/quotation/payment/claim is present.

P5-02: Admin 2's CREATE is acknowledged, then its dependent EDIT is interrupted before dispatch and the browser is disconnected. CREATE remains synced, EDIT pending; retry sends the same EDIT. Admin 1 independently retains an unacknowledged committed CREATE. Other profiles finish without waiting for them.

scenarios.scenario: Acknowledged operations never become new transactions on retry
scenarios.evidence: P5-02: a later manual sync after recovery produces zero additional sync POSTs for the acknowledged outboxes. P5-03/07: direct duplicate retries return original identities. P5-09/SQL retain acknowledgement/receipt identity across browser resumption.

scenarios.scenario: Two Admins edit the same request offline; stale conflict preserved
scenarios.evidence: P5-04: both download the same revision, queue distinct 18/19 quantities offline, then release EDITs together. Admin 2 wins with 19; Admin 1 gets 409 and retains quantity 18 plus the server version. An earlier retained race also preserves its losing operation and shows independent CREATEs behind that conflict still completing.

scenarios.scenario: Owner finalizes while an Admin has an older pending revision
scenarios.evidence: P5-05: Admin 4 queues quantity 99 offline; Owner saves ₹420 agreement and finalizes the server bill. Later Admin EDIT returns 409 with a closed server snapshot; quantity 99 remains local, server quantity 5/due 42,000 paise and finalization history remain unchanged.

scenarios.scenario: Competing Owner/Super Admin offline closures become explicit conflicts
scenarios.evidence: P5-06: both prepare the same agreed request revision, queue CLOSE offline and release together. Owner wins; Super Admin gets 409, keeps the provisional closure and closed server snapshot. Exactly one finalizer/account persists.

P5-07: a queued offline payment and three concurrent direct copies yield one ₹100 ledger entry/receipt. A real Admin-generated signed QR is accepted twice locally, retaining one HANDOVER; browser sync plus three copies retain one server claim/receipt/request. Signature independently verified. The late source CREATE becomes a preserved conflict rather than a second request.

P5-08: three payload scope mutations and two mismatched request-context submissions all return 409. Actual foreign request snapshot reads return 404 in both other-stall and other-active-season contexts despite explicit memberships. SQL confirms all new business writes stay in A/2026. Earlier phases' broader scope suites were not repeated.

scenarios.scenario: Actor, device, occurred_at and received_at metadata
scenarios.evidence: P5-01/09 and SQL: four distinct Admin/device identities; all 16 receipts match payload actor/device/captured role/occurrence time, acknowledgement revision and final operation audit event. Receipt/event received times are populated. Payment and QR creator/recipient device histories are independently validated.
